text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, four activities that previously ran in every trace run far less often: A27 in about 54 in 100 traces, and A36, A37 and A42 each in about 47–48 in 100, versus 200 of 200 traces before. A25, A26, A28 and A31 still run in every trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, POS003, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- A36, A37 and A42 now run only together: they co-occur in about 47 in 100 traces, in about 52–53 in 100 none of them runs, and traces with exactly one of them are virtually absent; before, all three co-occurred in every trace. [REL020, REL021, REL022]
- A27 and the A36/A37/A42 group became mutually exclusive. Before, A27 co-occurred with each of them in every trace, with the group running before A27 in about 99 in 100 cases; in the later window they co-occur in at most about 1 in 100 traces, with A27 alone in about 53 in 100 and the group alone in about 47 in 100. [REL011, REL012, REL013]
- Routing around this group changed. A25 now leads to A28 in about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, where before it split almost evenly over A36, A37 and A42 (about 35, 34 and 31 in 100). A26 now leads to A27 in about 53 in 100 and to A36, A37 or A42 in about 14–17 in 100 each, where before it led to A27 in about 98 in 100. Each group member now exits to A31 in about 28–36 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, where before the group exited mainly to A28. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- The group sits later in the trace: A36, A37 and A42 moved from a mean relative position of about 0.40 to about 0.58, while A28 (about 0.45 to 0.39) and A26 (about 0.60 to 0.54) moved earlier. [POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS002]
- Distances confirm the reordering. The A25→A28 gap collapsed from mostly 4 steps (about 94 in 100) to 1 step (about 99 in 100). The A26→A31 gap, previously almost always 2 steps (about 97 in 100), is now split between 2 steps (about 51 in 100) and 4 steps (about 46 in 100), matching the two trace groups. [LAG001, LAG005]
- Order relations are consistent with this: before, A36/A37/A42 ran before A26 in about 98–99 in 100 co-occurrences; in the later window A26 runs before them in every co-occurrence (about 46–47 in 100 of traces, with A26 alone otherwise). The group still runs before A31, and A28 still runs before A27 and before the group, whenever both are present. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL009, REL014, REL015, REL016]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the group A36/A37/A42 changed both its placement and how often it runs: in the later window, about 47 in 100 executions run the three activities together after A26 and before A31, without A27, while the remaining about 53 in 100 run A27 after A26 with none of the three; in every execution A25 is now directly followed by A28, whereas before, the group always ran between A25 and A28 and A27 always followed A26. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, LAG005]

This is a placement-and-routing hypothesis shown directly by relational evidence, not merely by frequency shifts: successor profiles at A25, A26 and the three group members changed, the order between A26 and the group flipped, A27 and the group became disjoint, and the two lag changes (A25→A28 shrinking from 4 steps to 1; A26→A31 splitting into 2 and 4 steps) reproduce the two trace groups almost exactly. Participation and position shifts corroborate the same split. The volume of findings also exceeds what an unchanged process produces: 50 items qualified where fewer than one was expected, and every difference is larger than in essentially all random re-splits of the pooled data. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL013, LAG001, LAG005, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, POS003, POS006, POS007, POS008]

Limitations: the windows are finite samples of 200 traces each, so the exact split (about 53 versus 47 in 100) and the small co-occurrence residuals carry sampling uncertainty, and differing variant frequencies between windows remain a competing explanation in principle — though an implausible one here, since each of these activities appeared in all 200 earlier traces, so a variant running in about half of the later traces cannot have been missed before. The internal order of A36/A37/A42 is mixed in both windows, so no fixed sequence inside the group is established, and several lag items on pairs spanning the group's old and new positions rest on a single observation and were not relied on. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011]
